headline: Partner at McKinsey & Company
about:
As a Partner at McKinsey & Company, I work closely with senior leadership teams across industries to address their most critical organizational challenges. My focus is on helping organizations reengineer, rethink, and reimagine how they lead, manage, and activate their talent to achieve transformative outcomes.

My expertise encompasses large-scale transformations, talent management, leadership development, and fostering high-performance cultures. I have a deep specialization in the implications of AI on talent and workforce dynamics, exploring how these advancements are reshaping the enterprise of the future. Additionally, I lead our thinking on Organizational Health, guiding organizations in building and operationalizing the behaviors required to foster a culture of energy, engagement, and sustainable performance.

I am deeply passionate about enabling individuals and organizations to realize their full potential and embrace meaningful change. I believe that the true power of leadership lies in inspiring and unlocking the potential of teams, empowering them to execute bold strategies with confidence. In an increasingly dynamic and agentic future, leaders must remain at the forefront of innovation and transformation, driving progress while fostering an environment where their teams can thrive and achieve extraordinary results.

experience.description:
Deep expert in Organizational Health and building a culture of performance. 

Organizational health is an organization’s capacity to deliver above-average financial and operating performance over time. It’s a measure of the mindsets, behaviors, and practices that happen day to day at work and indicative of how leadership leverage their resources to run the organization. By using our survey instrument – the Organizational Health Index (OHI) – coupled with 15+ years of research insights on 1500+ companies in our database, our team helps business leaders understand how their company actually gets things done. We combine this with a data-driven approach to prioritizing key focus areas and workshops to create a clear road map for how to improve organizational health.

Good organizational health translates into sustained performance. Healthy organizations outperform their unhealthy peers resulting in 3X greater total return to shareholders (TRS). What’s more, business leaders gain the tools to create and sustain the changes needed to drive long term performance.

about:
As a MBA Candidate at Chicago Booth, I am passionate about solving complex business problems and delivering impactful results for clients across various industries and regions. With concentrations in general strategy, finance, and entrepreneurship, I am pursuing strategic consulting as my post-MBA career path, while in parallel actively involved in supporting and advising small businesses and social ventures in Indonesia and Chicago.

Prior to Booth, I spent over a year as a Sales Finance Manager at Unilever, where I led and executed multiple strategic and operational projects in consumer products, digital transformation, financial analysis, and business finance model restructuring. I also collaborated with cross-functional and multicultural teams from India, Singapore, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Europe, honing my skills in team leadership and management. Additionally, I have received several awards and honors for my outstanding performance and achievements, such as the CFO Award, the 3rd Winner of the SKHA National Business Case Competition, and the First Winner of the National Audit Competition.

Outside of work and school, I am actively involved in empowering SMEs and early startups in Indonesia through IYS, a non-profit organization where I serve as a Board Member. I also share my insights and advice on career and personal development through webinars for students and fresh graduates in national universities across Indonesia. I believe in the power of education, innovation, and collaboration to create positive change and impact in society.

publications.title: Freeze-dried chitosan nanoparticles to stabilize and deliver bromelain
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Drug Delivery Science and Technology · Feb 1, 2021
publications.description: Bromelain has many therapeutic properties including wound healing and blood circulation improvement. However, bromelain is usually unstable and suffers autolysis, which results in a decrease of enzymatic activity and limited applications. Encapsulation of bromelain in nanoparticles can diminish degradation by protease immobilization, which may increase its stability and efficacy. The natural polymer chitosan can be nanostructured and trap the enzyme, maintaining the claims of biocompatibility, biodegradability and natural source of the formulation ingredients.

headline: McKinsey & Company | Global Supply Chain Leader | Operations | Lean | Change Agent | Continuous Improvement | People Leader
about:
I believe that supply chain & operations are the most vital part of any organization and can be used to improve the bottom line of the company and the experience of the customer.

I consider myself a business leader who focuses on supply chain, not an supply chain person; therefore, I approach everything in a business-minded way. Supply chain is not black and white; my job is to manage the ambiguity and expose the waste within processes for the benefit of the company, employees, and customers.

By proactively winning, advocating, investing in, and coaching key talent to drive growth, I help the company gain a larger return on its investments.

An inquisitive, proactive, collaborative and business-minded global supply chain leader, I am able to strategize, be analytical, and see the big picture but I am not afraid to roll up my sleeves and get hands-on with the details and the process. 

Known for excellent interpersonal and communication skills, which I believe are key to my success, I am able to gain credibility and build relationships quickly and effectively.

My business acumen, being able to come in and quickly learn the business and driving impact, value and growth almost immediately, is something that is often highlighted. 

Also known for my coaching abilities and my strong leadership capabilities, I am a change agent helping drive improvements for the betterment of the organization.

I posses a strong international background traveling, living, studying, and working around the world. I have worked in three countries (US, France, & Mexico) and have led teams global teams in South America, Europe, and Asia. I speak English, Spanish and French. 

I am passionate about the airline & tourism industries.

Talent Management, Performance Management, Business Strategy, Training, Change Management, Logistics, SAP, Excel VBA, Digital Implementations, Inventory Management, Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, Project Management, Strategic Sourcing, Management Consulting, #ONO

publications.title: Simul-frac Journey in the Permian Basin
publications.description: In 2019, the industry was approaching peak efficiency with standard zipper operations because the cost savings associated with cycle time reduction were offset by increased costs due to high friction pressures. Chevron trialed and fully implemented Simul-frac in the Permian Basin, which uses one frac crew to stimulate two wells simultaneously, to challenge the existing operational paradigm and improve cost and cycle time performance. This paper shares the Simul-frac journey including planning, execution, and lookbacks.

publications.title: Utilizing Managed Pressure Drilling to Overcome Narrow Margins During Liner Running and Cementing Operations
publications.description: In the past several years, managed pressure drilling (MPD) has developed from an emerging technology to become commonplace in many basins and fields. A joint operator / service company team has employed a technique that applies MPD methodology to cementing applications, increasing the probability of achieving successful primary cement jobs. This technique has been termed managed pressure cementing (MPC). This paper illustrates one of the first instances of successful implementation of MPC to run and cement a liner in the Gulf of Mexico (GOM).

projects.title: Kain Makna
projects.description:
Our initiative, MAKNA (/mak·na/), means purpose. This initiative is inspired by the Umutnana's women tenun community. Consisting of 20 village women, their work is to weave and produce tenun products. They used to have a ‘tenun-house’ that was rebuilt to become a health clinic (Puskesmas) due to not able to sell their products to a market or a distributor. These products are only available to sell whenever visitors come from the neighboring city of Kupang or given as gifts to government officials.

Solar Chapter will launch a brand and initiative named MAKNA—by Solar Chapter. MAKNA intends to approach the problem in a holistic way and therefore comprises of two aspects; education and commercialization by providing distribution channels and spreading awareness of Indonesia’s art of tenun. Solar Chapter plans to help Umutnana’s women sell their kain and promote their culture to young Indonesians living in cities, students studying abroad in the US and most importantly, exposing their beautiful art of into the world. For more information on MAKNA, visit our Instagram page, @kain.makna

about:
Jennifer currently services as Associate General Counsel and Global Legal Lead for Build by McKinsey, a newly formed division of McKinsey Digital. In this role she provides strategic, product, and commercial counsel to firm leaders focused on artificial intelligence, including GenAI, data analytics, technology product development, and blockchain.

As global managing counsel for the Accenture Technology Innovation legal team, Jennifer served as the strategic legal advisor for four interrelated business units—Ventures, Technology Labs, Liquid Studios, and Technology Incubation (Blockchain, Digital Currency & Cryptocurrency, Digital Assets, NFTs, Quantum, and Metaverse). As a technology transaction and product attorney she advised on wide-ranging legal issues including regulatory (antitrust, licensing, and industry-specific rules), data, IP, ethics, privacy, security, M&A due diligence / integration, marketing, export compliance, open source, procurement and other issues arising from new service and product offerings. She also focused on new technology risk evaluations working with the business to establish internal and go-to-market guardrails in emerging areas.

A member of Accenture’s legal team since 2007, Jennifer supported its pivot to technology innovation, incubation, and commercialization. She has negotiated 150+ deals with combined valued of $2.5+ billion, as well as global strategic relationships with alliance / vendor partners, research institutes and universities, and government funded agencies.

Jennifer created the cross-functional Global Legal Innovation Center of Excellence and Enablement Program for Accenture’s 150+ innovation locations worldwide and managed the Accenture Products and Platform commercial deal portfolio and product attorney legal team.

publications.title: Jos Fear & violence in central Nigeria in "Creed or Grievance: Muslim-Christian Relations and Conflict Resolution in Northern Nigeria"
publications.description: The violent politicization of religion has intermittently marked Jos, the capital of Plateau State, from 2001 to 2015. How this came to be, and how it is now gradually being overcome, is a lesson for many communities in northern Nigeria. Jos represented one of the most volatile ethno-religious conflicts in northern Nigeria. Since September 2001, there have been a series of destructive episodes of collective violence in Jos. While the rioting has not been continuous, it has divided much of the religiously plural city into Muslim and Christian areas and created a climate of fear and uncertainty.

publications.title: Jos - Bottom-up & top-down approaches to peace building in "Creed or Grievance: Muslim-Christian Relations and Conflict Resolution in Northern Nigeria"
publications.description: The protracted conflicts in Plateau State between 2001 and 2015 inevitably led to a series of efforts to achieve peace and, since 2015, some semblance of peace seems to have returned to Jos, albeit tentatively. This chapter examines the Jos peace processes. Specifically, it compares the efficacy of top-down and bottom-up approaches to peace building in Jos. We examine how individuals and neighbourhoods cope with insecurity at the bottom of society, and how state institutions – the Plateau State governments, and successive federal governments – have responded to the cycle of violence in Jos. At the community level, we show how the violence has re-shaped individuals’ social networks and accelerated the process of neighbourhood segregation. We examine how individuals and neighbourhoods seek safety through strategies of communal segregation and vigilantism, which have only started to be relaxed after 2015. At the state level, we examine the serial establishment of commissions of inquiry, both judicial and administrative, and the repeated inability to implement the recommendations of any. At the federal level, we examine the responses of the executive and legislature branches, and highlight the damaging tension between federal and state authorities in the management of the crises in Jos. Finally, we argue that Nigerian society has tended to approach the conflict in Jos through two opposed normative principles: (i) supporting inclusive civic citizenship which privileges the rights of individuals; or (ii) respecting the cultural and territorial rights of indigenous minority groups who are seen to be threatened by bigger and better-endowed ethnic groups. We argue that this binary approach – variously justified under the banner of individual rights or group rights – has played into the hands of intransigent and opportunistic politicians who have made it difficult to find a mutually agreeable route to peace.

headline: Problem Solver | Digital Transformation Specialist | MBA at Chicago Booth
about:
As a technology junkie, I embrace the digital transformation and change that is sweeping the world. Using my strategic thinking and experience with execution, I want to help companies find the most important levers of change to drive the most value. By blending the left (quantitative) and right (qualitative) sides of my brain, I help companies move faster into the future by blending the digital world with the physical world they live in. I have often been applauded for my creativity; however, I am most proud of my analytical skills. As a former engineer, I am highly analytical and able to dive deep into technology, processes, and details to understand how things work and what makes them tick. Leveraging my communication skills, I translate the most important takeaways and insights into digestible information so clients can focus on the most crucial elements of their business that drive value.

I have developed broad expertise while working with a range of companies spanning from large aircraft manufacturers to medical devices companies to makers of tiny electrical components. I also worked in the Electronics & High Tech and Industrial verticals performing various functions from creating new products to launching new markets. I enjoy working collaboratively on large projects and have led to a number of them that brought tangible value to either our company or the client. My leadership skills have also been tested by leading teams to first place in competitions, mentoring classmates, and building school culture teams that influence over 400 students each quarter.

When I’m not geeking out over the Hololens 2 or training for my next half marathon, you can find me on a plane itching to check off my next destination on my scratch-off world map.

projects.title: Independent Study: Comparative Analysis of Two-way Slabs Using ACI 318-11, IS 456:2000, EC2 BS EN 1992-1-1:2004, and ABNT NBR 6118:2014 Building Codes
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of Illinois at Chicago
projects.description: A thorough comparative analysis of the provisions for two-way slab design recorded in the American, Indian, European, and Brazilian Standards. Design provisions are described for flexure, shear, and deflection. In order to verify their validity and identify if any discrepancies occur, provisions are summarized in comparative tables and the same example is solved using each standard for flat slabs without beams. Building design code documents provide different methods, hence, their assumptions, limitations, and step-by-step procedures are described. Overall, it is observed that the EC2 is the most conservative one with a higher safety factor and a different approach for both flexural and shear reinforcement. ACI 318-11 and IS 456:2000 have an almost identical approach for flexure, while ABNT NBR 6118:2014 is the only code that does not provide separate provisions for flat slabs.

projects.description: This project focuses on developing a comprehensive urban transportation modeling system for the Chicago O'Hare International Airport with data collected by the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP). This report documents how the aviation system for metropolitan Chicago interacts with the surface transportation system, where employee trips and originating enplanements are discussed extensively.

volunteering.description:
Peru's Challenge aims to help local communities lift themselves out of poverty by giving them the resources required to grow sustainably. What they have found is that in all of the communities they have worked with so far, the locals know exactly what projects need to be implemented and how to implement them, and Peru's Challenge provides them with money and volunteers to help bring these projects to life. 

As a volunteer with Peru's Challenge, I specifically worked in the town of Quillahuata to help build a greenhouse for a local family so that they could make additional money growing and selling flowers. I saw firsthand that that local fathers had all the expertise required to build the greenhouse out of available materials, and I assisted in the construction by helping to lay the foundation, lay bricks, and erect the roof. Along with 6 other Michigan engineers and the help of the community, we were successfully able to complete our greenhouse project over a span of two weeks. The greenhouse can remain standing for up to 70 years so now the responsibility falls on the family and the community of Quillahuata to ensure that they sustain the work that has already been completed and use the additional revenue they gain from this greenhouse as a means of keeping their children in school and providing for other community improvement projects.

headline: McKinsey | UChicago PhD | Google Research Fellow | Global Health and Genetic Medicine
about:
My work is about implementing tractable scientific and technological solutions that enable everyone, everywhere, to live healthier lives. I am interested in combining my 10+ years of scientific, operational, and leadership experience to guide strategy development and implementation of global health initiatives, particularly projects with a focus on social impact, sustainability, and local capacity building.

In the past decade, the asymmetric health costs borne by disadvantaged populations have been brought to the forefront by the Ebola outbreak and more recently, by the COVID-19 pandemic. Systemic social inequalities account for much of this disparity, but a growing body of research has also demonstrated that genetic mechanisms contribute to differential risk and susceptibility to diseases. My PhD has been about characterizing the biological underpinnings of health disparities and expanding our understanding of human genetic diversity using an evolutionary lens.

Before graduate school, I was a research scientist and project manager at Harvard University working on infectious disease surveillance and outbreak response projects in West Africa (Nigeria and Senegal).

publications.title: Genome-wide association study identifies human genetic variants associated with fatal outcome from Lassa fever
publications.description: Infection with Lassa virus (LASV) can cause Lassa fever, a haemorrhagic illness with an estimated fatality rate of 29.7%, but causes no or mild symptoms in many individuals. Here, to investigate whether human genetic variation underlies the heterogeneity of LASV infection, we carried out genome-wide association studies (GWAS) as well as seroprevalence surveys, human leukocyte antigen typing and high-throughput variant functional characterization assays. We analysed Lassa fever susceptibility and fatal outcomes in 533 cases of Lassa fever and 1,986 population controls recruited over a 7 year period in Nigeria and Sierra Leone. We detected genome-wide significant variant associations with Lassa fever fatal outcomes near GRM7 and LIF in the Nigerian cohort. We also show that a haplotype bearing signatures of positive selection and overlapping LARGE1, a required LASV entry factor, is associated with decreased risk of Lassa fever in the Nigerian cohort but not in the Sierra Leone cohort. Overall, we identified variants and genes that may impact the risk of severe Lassa fever, demonstrating how GWAS can provide insight into viral pathogenesis.

publications.title: Combining genomics and epidemiology to track mumps virus transmission in the United States
publications.description: Unusually large outbreaks of mumps across the United States in 2016 and 2017 raised questions about the extent of mumps circulation and the relationship between these and prior outbreaks. We paired epidemiological data from public health investigations with analysis of mumps virus whole genome sequences from 201 infected individuals, focusing on Massachusetts university communities. Our analysis suggests continuous, undetected circulation of mumps locally and nationally, including multiple independent introductions into Massachusetts and into individual communities. Despite the presence of these multiple mumps virus lineages, the genomic data show that one lineage has dominated in the US since at least 2006. Widespread transmission was surprising given high vaccination rates, but we found no genetic evidence that variants arising during this outbreak contributed to vaccine escape. Viral genomic data allowed us to reconstruct mumps transmission links not evident from epidemiological data or standard single-gene surveillance efforts and also revealed connections between apparently unrelated mumps outbreaks.

publications.title: Genomic Analysis of Lassa Virus during an Increase in Cases in Nigeria in 2018
publications.publishedAt: The New England Journal of Medicine · Oct 17, 2018
publications.description: During 2018, an unusual increase in Lassa fever cases occurred in Nigeria, raising concern among national and international public health agencies. We analyzed 220 Lassa virus genomes from infected patients, including 129 from the 2017–2018 transmission season, to understand the viral populations underpinning the increase. A total of 14 initial genomes from 2018 samples were generated at Redeemer’s University in Nigeria, and the findings were shared with the Nigerian Center for Disease Control in real time. We found that the increase in cases was not attributable to a particular Lassa virus strain or sustained by human-to-human transmission. Instead, the data were consistent with ongoing cross-species transmission from local rodent populations. Phylogenetic analysis also revealed extensive viral diversity that was structured according to geography, with major rivers appearing to act as barriers to migration of the rodent reservoir.

publications.title: Field-deployable viral diagnostics using CRISPR-Cas13
publications.description: Mitigating global infectious disease requires diagnostic tools that are sensitive, specific, and rapidly field deployable. In this study, we demonstrate that the Cas13-based SHERLOCK (specific high-sensitivity enzymatic reporter unlocking) platform can detect Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) in patient samples at concentrations as low as 1 copy per microliter. We developed HUDSON (heating unextracted diagnostic samples to obliterate nucleases), a protocol that pairs with SHERLOCK for viral detection directly from bodily fluids, enabling instrument-free DENV detection directly from patient samples in <2 hours. We further demonstrate that SHERLOCK can distinguish the four DENV serotypes, as well as region-specific strains of ZIKV from the 2015–2016 pandemic. Finally, we report the rapid (<1 week) design and testing of instrument-free assays to detect clinically relevant viral single-nucleotide polymorphisms.

publications.title: Zika virus evolution and spread in the Americas
publications.description: Although the recent Zika virus (ZIKV) epidemic in the Americas and its link to birth defects have attracted a great deal of attention, much remains unknown about ZIKV disease epidemiology and ZIKV evolution, in part owing to a lack of genomic data. Here we address this gap in knowledge by using multiple sequencing approaches to generate 110 ZIKV genomes from clinical and mosquito samples from 10 countries and territories, greatly expanding the observed viral genetic diversity from this outbreak. We analysed the timing and patterns of introductions into distinct geographic regions; our phylogenetic evidence suggests rapid expansion of the outbreak in Brazil and multiple introductions of outbreak strains into Puerto Rico, Honduras, Colombia, other Caribbean islands, and the continental United States. We find that ZIKV circulated undetected in multiple regions for many months before the first locally transmitted cases were confirmed, highlighting the importance of surveillance of viral infections. We identify mutations with possible functional implications for ZIKV biology and pathogenesis, as well as those that might be relevant to the effectiveness of diagnostic tests.

publications.title: Genomic epidemiology reveals multiple introductions of Zika virus into the United States
publications.description: Zika virus (ZIKV) is causing an unprecedented epidemic linked to severe congenital abnormalities. In July 2016, mosquito-borne ZIKV transmission was reported in the continental United States; since then, hundreds of locally acquired infections have been reported in Florida. To gain insights into the timing, source, and likely route(s) of ZIKV introduction, we tracked the virus from its first detection in Florida by sequencing ZIKV genomes from infected patients and Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. We show that at least 4 introductions, but potentially as many as 40, contributed to the outbreak in Florida and that local transmission is likely to have started in the spring of 2016—several months before its initial detection. By analysing surveillance and genetic data, we show that ZIKV moved among transmission zones in Miami. Our analyses show that most introductions were linked to the Caribbean, a finding corroborated by the high incidence rates and traffic volumes from the region into the Miami area. Our study provides an understanding of how ZIKV initiates transmission in new regions.

publications.title: Offspring sex preferences among patrilineal and matrilineal Mosuo in Southwest China revealed by differences in parity progression
publications.description: Son preference predominates in China, yet there are patterned exceptions to this rule. In this paper, we test whether lineality (patrilineal versus matrilineal inheritance and descent) is associated with son versus daughter preference among the ethnic Mosuo (Na) of Southwest China. Our results show (i) an increased probability of continued fertility among matrilineal women after having a son compared with a daughter and (ii) an increased probability of continued fertility among patrilineal women after having a daughter compared with a son. These results are consistent with son preference among patrilineal Mosuo and more muted daughter preference among the matrilineal Mosuo. Furthermore, we show (iii) the lowest probability of continued fertility at parity 2 once women have one daughter and one son across both systems, suggesting that preferences for at least one of each sex exist alongside preferences for the lineal sex. The Mosuo are the only known small-scale society in which two kinship systems distinguish sub-groups with many otherwise shared cultural characteristics. We discuss why this, in conjunction with differences in subsistence, may shed light on the evolutionary underpinnings of offspring sex preferences.

headline: Public Sector Expert at McKinsey & Company
about:
I am passionate about creation of social impacts through raising key questions, identifying key issues to be addressed, designing projects to pull key levers, and delivering hands-on works with clients.

My focus has been mainly on health, ranging from health policy (medical, long-term care, prevention), pandemic resilience, globalizing Japan’s health, medical institutions transformation (strategy finance, operation, IT (EMR, AI adaptation, etc.), data analytics, HR, supply and architecture), medical data (NDB, DPC, etc.), innovation and technologies (medical device, health services and products), investment advisory (VC/PE), workstyle reform of medical and clinical professionals to fundamental life sciences like whole-genome analysis.
Among these, three highlights are: (1) establishment of a best practice operational model for leading acute hospitals (e.g., productivity improvement of up to 30-40%); (2) construction of the national long-term care prevention system with end-to-end consultation; and (3) launch of the physician workstyle reform review organization by building consensus among academic societies and key stakeholders.

In addition to my experience in Japan, I have also worked in the US, UK, India and Uzbekistan. In my internship at PwC US, I was engaged in a quite large-scale hospital financial recovery project, where I provide Japan’s best practice in 8 work streams, which resulted in creation of a white paper on comparison of hospital transformation methods between US and Japan. My experience in the UK encompassed: (1) advisory for a healthcare-specialized VC and (2) consultancy to health product venture. In India, I led a strategic project for a US leading medical device company on its market entry. The project I sourced in Uzbekistan was for a cotton yarn company’s new exploration support as well as its manufacturing excellence. 

With respect to my academic background, on top of the Master of Science in Physics at University of Tokyo (organic superconductor), I acquired MBA at Cambridge Judge Business School for fostering my business perspectives, then recently I have been equipped also with PhD in Medicine at Tokyo Medical and Dental University for sophisticating my expertise in health.

experience.description: Leading public sector advisory business on health policy and management.
I lead the healthcare business, and serving as a job manager in socially important engagements, such as a series of landmark projects in Osaka.

I have developed high value scheme for hospital consulting scheme, which have been seen quite difficult because of hospital's low profitability by the tight medical cost control by the government.  In addition, I have established and utilized consulting methodologies for performance improvement, such as Quick Assessment, PFM (Patient Flow Management) and Sama Day Diagnosis.

I have started post-MBA career at PwC Japan.  I am going to be engaged in turnaround business to Japanese and foreign clients suffering from severe financial difficulty.  With utilizing PwC's local and global specialists, our team will serve a wide variety of high-quality consultation and information service.

I have participated in an internship program that was specially arranged by PwC Global and Japan.  In the program, I was assigned to a PwC's brand-defining project, the total turnaround engagement project for a large-scale public health system in the Midwest.  My mission was to make a comparative study on hospital transformation methodologies in the United States and Japan.  Comparing PwC's highly sophisticated and established advisory schemes and Japan's best practice hospital's distinctive reform methods was exceedingly useful for considering innovative future methodology for both PwC U.S. and Japan.  Through this great opportunity, I could learn that hospital reform plays a vital role in the both countries' health reform, and that commonly indispensable factor is productivity improvement.  The results of this comparative study provided both the United States and Japan with new strategies for further hospital productivity improvement.  As to implications to Japan's hospital, I myself will try to establish an innovative methodology at PwC Japan from February 2011.

Conducted a strategic consulting project to NOVASPIN, a company headquartered in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. The NOVASPIN's main issue was the rise of the material cost (raw cotton price). In order for the client to overcome this difficulty, I dedicated to researching on what strategy can be applied and how they can manage it. With having intensive study on the international cotton supply chain in the area of middle asia, I also conducted field work in Tashkent, visiting plant and interviewing with NOVASPIN's management. The final recommendation included further entry strategy to Russian and the east European markets, and was featured by reinforcement of alliance relationship with lower-stream businesses in those emerging markets.

In the program of Cambridge Judge Business School, I have experienced precious opportunities, such as a consulting project to venture healthcare company, strategic consulting project to Indian headquarter of US medical device company, research project for promoting healthcare venture capital, which is now facing a turning point, and etc.

It was also great for me to travel to Istanbul, Athens, Venice, Munich and Paris on the way from New Dehli to London, because of the volcanic erruption in Iceland. I could understand cultural difference and connection between those countries, and realized that mutual succeeding of each culture, technology, and political and economic system among countries around Mediterranean Sea was the very source of the current western civilization.

I investigated the impact of the UK's health reform on hospital management, with utilizing my knowledge and experience in Japan's health reform. 

The most significant advantage of UK health system is, in my view, that it adapts budget limit. Due to that, the medical expenditure remains lower than that in other developed countries. The downside is that this system makes it difficult to get information for efficiency improvement. In the US or Japan, profitability is clear and much more critical for hospital, and it could also be the major indicator for promoting efficiency improvement. In the UK, not profitability but wait time is the major indicator. But it seems that this operational indicator does not necessarily have enough power to drastically change hospital management, but rather it has more to do with quality of medicine. The recent introduction of the tariff will breakthrough this situation, but, as of now, it is still on basic stage and not suitable for cost accounting by disease. I would like to follow how the tariff will evolve from now on.

Venture capital business is now highly interested in healthcare and life-science area, where new technologies are emerging, such as regenerative medicine.  The mission of this project was to research promising new products or new technologies that VC should consider eager investment in the near future.  My recommendation was on potential technologies that could be related to stroke prediction, which would be able to reduce social costs by untimely care for stroke.

Thanks to my ex-client in Japan, I could source this project. The project is to a Indian headquarter of a US leading medical device company, Stryker. Our task was to create the strategy to promote Stryker's highly sophisticated and high value product, which is already popular in the US and Europe, in Indian market, which is highly cost-sensitive.

Through this project, I could understand what is needed in the emerging market and how global companies should promote its high value product. Also, I learned in greater detail regarding the current situation of Indian healgh.

While my stay in India, I visited Agra, the city of Taji Mahal, and Jaisalmer. Taji Mahal is, not to mention, the most beautiful historial building in the world. In addition, Jaisalmer, where I stayed in a palace like hotel and visited so many Jain temples, is very nice place to learn how Indian culture is related to middle east asian culture.

Mitsubishi Research Institute is a profit-making, independent think tank, which was founded in 1970. It conducts approximately 2,000 research and consulting projects annually mainly to central governments in wide range of areas including healthcare and social security.

My business was mainly to make policy related research for the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) and serve as the secretariat in expert committees held by MHLW. Also, I conducted model project initiated by MHLW, such as a project to promote regional preventive care for elderly people. In that project, our team facilitated expert committee consisted of medical and statistics professionals, conducted nationwide research, and managed nearly 100 municipal governments so that they can try the new system. Organizations that affect Japan's policy making could also be my client. For example, in a project to an American medical device industry association, I conducted an international comparative research on the cost structure of medical device in the US, UK, France, Germany and Japan, and, based on the results, held a forum for leading media companies for advocating what Japan should do for the problem called 'device lag.'

I have delivered management consulting service to more than 10 acute hospitals in Japan. My task included turnaround overall hospital management, improvement of operational efficiency, reform of procurement, and etc.

I have two quite significant experiences for the whole Japan's health system.
Firstly, I made the Japan's best practice hospital, in which I realized productivity improvement by up to 40%. Although productivity improvement is regarded as almost impossible in this field, I showed it is possible. I am convinced that this landmark case could be the key to streamlining Japan's too many hospitals.
Secondly, I contributed to construct a medical device group purchasing system in a private hospital group, and realized 10% reduction of its medical device procurement cost and 30% profit margin to my department. Group purchasing of medical device is not popular in Japan (I think our case is the first/early trial in Japan) and hence there will be much room to be applied.

location.linkedinText: New York, New York, United States

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

about:
Julia Steyn is currently Chief Commercial Officer at VectoIQ – an investment firm specializing in special situation investments in mobility space.   An innovative thought leader in transportation, Julia Steyn had almost a decade long career at General Motors where she was Vice President of Global Corporate Development and M&A, as well as the founder and CEO of Maven, the shared mobility marketplace owned by General Motors.  

Julia Steyn is currently a Non-Executive Board Member of Garrett Motion Inc., Nasdaq listed leader in turbocharging, electric boosting and automotive software solutions. She also serves on Metalsa Board of Directors, private company leading in automotive structures for heavy and light trucks.  Julia is also a member of Commonwealth Rolling Products Board of Directors owned by American Industrial Partners and specializing in automotive rolling products.   In addition, Julia is a Senior Advisor to McKinsey with a focus on the mobility space and corporate innovation. In addition, Julia serves as an advisor to several venture capital organizations.  Previously, Julia also serves as a Non-Executive Board Member of First Group PLC in London, UK, a multi-national transport group that operates transport services in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada and the United States.  

Earlier in her career, Julia was vice president and co-managing director for Alcoa's Corporate Development group, leading its mergers and acquisitions, competitive scanning and new business target screening activities.  She also has worked at Goldman Sachs in key positions in London, Moscow and New York. Her responsibilities included a broad variety of transactions across a number of countries, industries and products. Earlier in her career, she was a business analyst at A.T. Kearney.
 
Julia has a bachelor’s degree from Oberlin College in Oberlin, Ohio, and an MBA with a concentration in Finance and Accounting from the University of Chicago. She also was a concert pianist of international distinction. She was born in Russia and moved to the U.S. in 1990.

In addition, Steyn was a concert pianist of international distinction. She was born in Russia and moved to the U.S. in 1990.  Continuing with her passion for classic music, Julia is currently serving as Young Associate Director at the Metropolitan Opera Board.

headline: Senior Partner and Co-Leader of McKinsey's Mergers & Acquisitions Practice.  Previously Co-Leader of Life Sciences; Advisor to Pharma, BioTech and Medical Device leaders strategy, M&A, R&D, commercial and operations
about:
I’m a Senior Partner at McKinsey & Company and leader of the Firm’s Mergers & Acquisitions in the Americas and co-leader globally.  Previously I served as the leader of the Life Sciences Practice in North America and co-leader globally.  I have extensive experience counseling CEOs and Boards on topics of corporate strategy, portfolio management, M&A, separations and spins, divestitures, and JVs and alliances.  I have more than 20 years of experience advising CEOs and leaders of pharmaceutical and medical-technology companies on topics including corporate strategy, growth strategy, commercial execution, international expansion, mergers and acquisitions, risk management, and operational excellence. I also advise private-equity companies seeking opportunities in healthcare mergers and acquisitions. With a background in biomechanical and mechanical engineering, I’ve helped many of the world’s leading providers of medical devices and biotechnologies understand the potential impact of changing technology on the value chain and patient care. I am committed to innovating every aspect of healthcare and inspired by the impact we as an industry have on patients and those that care for them.  I frequently speak about changes in US healthcare at conferences and panels across North America, and the challenges of scaling biotech companies. 
I previously led the Chicago Office and am deeply embedded in the Chicago Community.  A proud Chicagoan, I’m active in my community, currently serving on the board of Boys and Girls Club of Chicago.  Previously I served on the boards of both the Civic Consulting Alliance and tourism organization, Choose Chicago. Before joining McKinsey, I held technical roles at various companies and gained my PhD in Engineering at Duke University.  I currently serve on the Board of Visitors of the Pratt School of Engineering at Duke University.  I enjoy downhill skiing, paddle tennis, golf, wine tasting.  Having grown up in Wisconsin, I am an avid Green Bay Packers fan.

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: March 14, 2016, Kate was Laura’s client
receivedRecommendations.description:
I joined Laura's Serious Play workshop in Amsterdam, November 2015, because it appealed to my rational, business-side while teasing the latent, not-always conscious creative side in me.  I'd been in serious myopic life mode - thinking linearly about my life.  I thought Serious Play could give me the time, space and creative angle(s) to think anew about what was important to me.   

I'd recommend going into the workshop with no expectations.  
Laura introduces a series of exercises for getting you out of your head and to be present in the "here and now" in order to enforce present-moment being/thinking.
At the beginning, you don't know where the exercises are leading.
There is significant time to journal and write down "now" moments and thoughts.
In fact, that part of the workshop was completely unexpected and yet, extremely rewarding.
The free-flow of thoughts and ideas was liberating; fascinating; enlightening.
A couple hours into the workshop and most definitely, on the second day, I came to welcome the physical forms of exercise - they were fun, fanciful, the kid-in-you inducing.  

The methodologies that Laura utilizes to get you out of your logical/rational/analytical mind and into free-flow creative was exactly what made me feel good.  The reinforcement that Creative is not something related to creative-type people but is in fact, native in all of use coupled with the idea that tapping Creative thought can be done using methodologies taught and practiced in Laura's Serious Play workshop, was literally, an eye-popping, holly-Jesus serendipitous epiphany.  I mean, who would have thunk that you can tap the Creative in you by using Methods so simple and effective?  

Post-workshop, I felt energized, relaxed, open to new opportunities and importantly, able to see many multiple paths for moving forward. I felt more alive with possibilities that were most definitely in my reach.  If you want to experience a different way or thinking; a different way of being, go take Laura's workshop. It's as simple as that.
